entities.name: Alain Paul Lebeaupin
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alain Paul Lebeaupin (b. 1950) is a French Catholic bishop who served as a senior Vatican diplomat, including as Apostolic Nuncio to the European Union in Brussels. Ordained a priest of the Diocese of Coutances, he entered the Vatican diplomatic service and rose to significant positions representing the Holy See in European institutional contexts.

Lebeaupin's appointment as Apostolic Nuncio to the European Union made him the Holy See's principal interlocutor with one of the world's most important supranational governance bodies. The EU-Holy See relationship involves questions of religious freedom, human rights, education, family policy, and the role of religious values in public life—areas of significant Catholic concern in the secular European project.

His career in Vatican diplomacy exemplifies the Holy See's distinctive approach to international relations: maintaining formal diplomatic presence in both state-based and supranational institutions, engaging European governance on values questions, and representing the interests of Catholics across the European Union's member states. His French background gave him particular cultural resources for engaging Franco-centric European political culture.
